item.title: Dein Weg zu Bitcoin – Michael Saylor im Orange Jacket – Abu über Bitcoin & Mut im Unternehmertum – Dein Weg zu Bitcoin
item.description:
Abu habe ich vor zwei Jahren im Bitcoin-Hotel in Plochingen kennengelernt, und seitdem schaue ich ihm fasziniert zu. Er hat mit BitArt eine der ersten Bitcoin-Kunstgalerien Europas gegründet, mit 21Million Fashion ein Bitcoin-Modelabel aufgebaut und in Abu Dhabi Michael Saylor sein eigenes Orange Jacket überreicht. Einen Plan dafür gab es nie. Was es immer gab, war eine Vision und den Mut, einfach loszugehen.Was passiert, wenn du einem Traum folgst, für den es keinen Bauplan gibt?👉 Wie Abu nach einem Jahr Vorarbeit 15 Sekunden mit Michael Saylor bekam und warum die Jacke auf Anhieb passte👉 Warum Proof of Work für ihn auch Handwerk, Stoffe und echte Qualität beschreibt👉 Was ein Cappuccino 2017 in Sats gekostet hat und was heute👉 Wie Hameln Bitcoin in die Stadt bringen will, bis hin zu einer Bibliothek, beheizt mit Mining-Abwärme👉 Warum Scheitern kein Scheitern istMich hat in diesem Gespräch vor allem eins berührt: Abu redet nicht über Erfolg, sondern über den Weg dorthin. Über schlechte Tage, an denen er alles hinschmeißen will. Über Samen, die er streut, ohne zu wissen, welcher aufgeht.„Vision ohne Aktion ist Halluzination.“ – Abu

🔗 LinksAbu: https://www.instagram.com/abullishonbitcoin/21 Million Fashion: https://www.21million-fashion.com/Weser-Wirtschaftsforum: https://wwforum.org/Zukunftsdialog Hameln: 10. Juni 2027✨ Mein Ziel: Bitcoin verständlich machen – mit Geschichten, die zeigen, dass die ersten Schritte nicht groß sein müssen.👍 Gefällt dir die Folge? Abonnieren, liken und an jemanden schicken, der das hören sollte. Fragen und Meinungen gern in die Kommentare – ich lese alle!⚡ Audio-Version & Sats per Lightning senden auf Fountain: https://fountain.fm/show/WdHajypwLY2JOQN2zH1SHier findest du mich:📲 Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/finanz.bewusstsein 🔗 FinanzBewusst: https://finanzbewusst.com/🧡 Partner (Code FINANZB)Coinfinity – Bitcoin kaufen, 21 % weniger Gebühren für 6 Monate: https://coinfinity.co/bitcoin-appBitcoin21 – Kleidung, 10 %: https://bitcoin21.shop/?ref=FINANZB21statues – Lampen & Statuen, 5 %: https://21statues.de?sca_ref=10285598.SH2VZ7SHVa8BitBox – Cold Wallet, 5 %: https://shop.bitbox.swiss/?ref=tfjnborqSeedor – Stahl-Backup, 5 %: https://www.seedor.io/discount/FINANZBBitUcation – Bitcoin-Bildung: https://bitucation.com/Was ich trage:⚪️Bitcoin21 Oversized T-Shirt: https://bitcoin21.shop/products/bitcoin-oversized-t-shirt?ref=FINANZBRechtlicher Hinweis: Dieser Podcast dient der finanziellen Bildung und persönlichen Meinungsäußerung und ist keine Finanz- oder Anlageberatung. item.title: The Bitcoin Matrix – Aaron Siri: The One Product You Can't Sue in America
item.description:
"People say 'I believe in vaccines.' Nobody says that about seatbelts."

Aaron Siri is the managing partner of Siri & Glimstad and, by most measures, the most consequential vaccine litigator in America. He's the attorney behind the famous nine-hour deposition of Dr. Stanley Plotkin — the man they call the godfather of vaccines — lead counsel for the Informed Consent Action Network (ICAN), a 2025 Senate witness, and a central legal figure in the RFK-era reshaping of federal vaccine policy. His new book is Vaccines, Amen: The Religion of Vaccines — in his words, "a cross-examination in book form."

This one steps outside the show's usual lane, and I want to be upfront: this is not medical advice, I'm not a doctor, and everything Aaron argues here is his own case — where it's contested by public-health bodies, treat it as one side of an open debate. What ties it to this show is the question we always ask: how do you know what's real when you're not allowed to check? From there we go deep — how a custody case led to the legendary Plotkin deposition; the Hepatitis B shot Aaron says was licensed on a trial of 147 kids, five days of monitoring, and no control group; the 1986 law he calls "the original sin" that handed vaccine makers liability immunity; the Ford Pinto and what punitive damages actually do; informed consent versus the right to refuse; whether vaccines really stop transmission; and the measles-mortality data he argues almost no one talks about. A conversation about evidence, incentives, and who gets to audit the people in charge.

Subscribe so you never miss an episode.

item.itunes:summary:
"People say 'I believe in vaccines.' Nobody says that about seatbelts."

Aaron Siri is the managing partner of Siri & Glimstad and, by most measures, the most consequential vaccine litigator in America. He's the attorney behind the famous nine-hour deposition of Dr. Stanley Plotkin — the man they call the godfather of vaccines — lead counsel for the Informed Consent Action Network (ICAN), a 2025 Senate witness, and a central legal figure in the RFK-era reshaping of federal vaccine policy. His new book is Vaccines, Amen: The Religion of Vaccines — in his words, "a cross-examination in book form."

This one steps outside the show's usual lane, and I want to be upfront: this is not medical advice, I'm not a doctor, and everything Aaron argues here is his own case — where it's contested by public-health bodies, treat it as one side of an open debate. What ties it to this show is the question we always ask: how do you know what's real when you're not allowed to check? From there we go deep — how a custody case led to the legendary Plotkin deposition; the Hepatitis B shot Aaron says was licensed on a trial of 147 kids, five days of monitoring, and no control group; the 1986 law he calls "the original sin" that handed vaccine makers liability immunity; the Ford Pinto and what punitive damages actually do; informed consent versus the right to refuse; whether vaccines really stop transmission; and the measles-mortality data he argues almost no one talks about. A conversation about evidence, incentives, and who gets to audit the people in charge.

Subscribe so you never miss an episode.

item.title: Swan Signal Live - A Bitcoin Show – John Haar Returns: Why the Fed Must Talk Tough While It Inflates
item.description:
• John reads Warsh's Jackson Hole speech as a nothing burger for Bitcoiners: a Fed chair must talk tough on inflation because signaling anything else would send inflation expectations and yields higher, while the long-run path of financial repression stays the same
  • Warsh reported that 54% of PCE basket components rose more than 3% over the past year, called 4.1% unemployment full employment, and framed inflation as squarely the Fed's problem to solve
  • Markets read the speech as hawkish anyway: the two-year yield rose about 12 basis points while gold and Bitcoin each gave back roughly 3.5%
  • On last week's expanded Treasury buybacks, John points to two signals: a 30-year yield near 5.3% is clearly bothering policymakers, and the Fed has never meaningfully reduced its holdings of 10-year-plus Treasuries even during quantitative tightening, evidence that natural buyers of long-dated government paper are scarce
  • The hosts revisit the shallowest bear market thesis they developed together on this show: a roughly 52% drawdown against 77% to 90%-plus in prior cycles, with the June low of $58,000 sitting just below the 200-week moving average before price rocketed back through it
  • John explains why he believes the June low will hold, while framing the 50-week moving average near $82,000 as the level the market is watching to declare a new bull market
  • Glassnode data shows 1.05 million Bitcoin of long-term holder supply with a cost basis between $83,000 and $86,000, the first heavy resistance shelf above spot, and the hosts discuss how cost basis shapes market psychology
  • The debasement trade is back in ETF volumes, with GLD and IBIT both in the top ten most traded funds, and the Bitcoin-to-gold ratio breaking its year-long downtrend after gold's 2025 outperformance
  • Bitcoin's long correlation with software stocks broke down in June, and John argues it was always the wrong frame, a point Lyn Alden's Wall Street Journal essay makes at length: Bitcoin is a protocol of value, not another technology stock
  • A broad Treasury ETF has returned roughly negative 18% after inflation over fifteen years while the supply of government debt keeps expanding, the picture John says is quietly ending the era of Treasuries as the world's default store of value

item.description:
von Cory Klippsten – Originaltitel: «The World Bitcoin Will Build«

«Niemand wird unsere ‚Bright Orange Future‘ für uns machen.
Wir müssen es selbst tun.»

(Cory Klippsten)

«Fix the money, fix the world.» Repariere das Geldsystem –
repariere die Welt. Das weltweit erste und größte dezentrale Geldnetzwerk könnte eine lebendigere und gerechtere Gesellschaft einleiten. In welcher Hinsicht und in welchen Zeiträumen der Autor dies erwartet, könnt Ihr in dieser übersetzten Vorlesung seines Artikels hören, die gleichzeitig auch ein wenig auf die symbolträchtige Vorlesung Nr. 210 vorbereitet. ;-)

item.title: The Bitcoin Layer – Wall Street Has No Idea What the Fed Is Doing Anymore
item.description: <![CDATA[In this episode, Nik covers the Fed’s decision to hold and the reaction that surprised him more than the decision itself: Bloomberg’s anchors in full meltdown over how Kevin Warsh is communicating. He walks through their three complaints, the dissents, Warsh declining to explain why the Fed didn’t hike, and the suggestion that Williams and Jefferson are really setting policy. Nik explains why he thinks the hold was justified given how much conditions tightened after September, and why Warsh believes higher rates will slow the AI buildout. He closes on bitcoin’s four price drivers and why a steepening yield curve could relieve some pressure.]]>

item.title: bitcoin ist - Wissen statt FOMO – 24) ... Energie mit zwei Leben
item.description:
Bitcoin und Energieverbrauch werden oft in einem negativen Zusammenhang genannt. Diese Folge zeigt ein differenzierteres Bild: warum Bitcoin-Mining Stromnetze stabilisieren kann, wie aus Abwärme ein zweiter Wertschöpfungskreislauf entsteht, und wo die Grenzen dieser Entwicklung aktuell noch liegen.

Themen in dieser Folge:

  • Wie sich der Anteil nachhaltiger Energien beim Bitcoin-Mining seit 2022 entwickelt hat
  • Warum der Ausbau von Wind- und Solarenergie ein Netzstabilitätsproblem mit sich bringt
  • Wie Bitcoin-Miner als flexible Last genutzt werden können, um Lastspitzen abzupuffern
  • Warum jede Kilowattstunde beim Mining "zwei Leben" bekommt: Bitcoin-Belohnung und nutzbare Wärme
  • Drei Unternehmen, die das bereits umsetzen: Terahash, 21energy und Power2Bit


Die Anfangs erwähnte Studie der Cambridge University

https://www.jbs.cam.ac.uk/2025/cambridge-study-sustainable-energy-rising-in-bitcoin-mining/


Erwähnte Unternehmen:

  • Terahash – Bitcoin-Mining Infrastruktur für Unternehmen
  • 21energy – Bitcoin-Heizungen für Privathaushalte und Kleingewerbe
  • Power2Bit – flexible, klimaneutrale Rechenzentren und kommunale Wärmeplanung


Hinweis: Die genannten Prozentzahlen zum Energiemix variieren je nach Berechnungsmethode (konservativer Netzmix vs. direkte Unternehmensmeldungen) und waren zum Zeitpunkt der Aufnahme aktuell.

]]>

item.title: Bitcoin News Alerts | Daily BTC Macro Signal – 2499: $400,000 Bitcoin LIQUIDITY SHOCK - The Fed's Money Printer Is About to FLIP
item.description:
BITCOIN TO $400,000! America's $40 TRILLION debt crisis could be creating the perfect conditions for an unprecedented Bitcoin bull market. With the Federal Reserve confronting mounting fiscal pressure and Bitcoin's supply permanently limited to 21 million coins, the monetary system faces a fundamental contradiction: governments can create more currency, but nobody can create more Bitcoin beyond its programmed limit.

In today's episode of Bitcoin News Alerts, we examine the numbers behind the $400K Bitcoin thesis. At an illustrative 4% interest rate, $40 trillion in debt represents $1.6 trillion in annual interest costs. Meanwhile, Bitcoin miners produce approximately 450 new BTC daily, and a hypothetical 1% allocation from $230 trillion in institutional capital would represent $2.3 trillion in potential demand.

We also explore Michael Saylor's Bitcoin accumulation strategy, corporate treasury adoption, institutional demand, and why Bitcoin's fixed supply could become increasingly valuable as monetary pressures intensify.

📺 Prefer video? Watch daily Bitcoin breakdowns: http://BitcoinNewsAlerts.net

]]>

Sam Baker, research analyst at River, joins me to explain why Bitcoin could reach $840,000 within the next three to five years. item.title: The Café Bitcoin Podcast – The Finale: Liquid's 4,000 Bitcoin, the Caching Bug, and 50 Days for Freedom Wrapped
item.description:
• The last day. Brady opened with the count, 37 shows in 50 days, and the campaign's frame: political independence 250 years ago, monetary independence now. Yan Pritzker, Frank Corva, Suze and Alec on stage; Unseen Finance returned at the end.
  • The Liquid hack, plainly. On Sunday somebody sent 4,000 L-BTC to SideSwap's peg-out and the Liquid Federation paid out real Bitcoin. The L-BTC had been created from nothing. Blockstream paused the sidechain and 3,400 Bitcoin came back Monday.
  • ⭐ Yan on what broke: a caching bug, not anyone's keys. "The only two hard problems in computer science are naming and cache invalidation." Two transactions shared one cache key, so validators mistook a fake for one already checked.
  • Why it is not Bitcoin. Yan: Liquid is an 11-of-15 federation of companies with its own database and rules. "This is a separate thing, this is not Bitcoin itself." Lightning is built on Bitcoin script; Liquid is not.
  • ⭐ Frank on the 15%. The hackers returned 85% and kept about 600 Bitcoin. His question: will anyone be made whole, and if they keep it, "they're surely not white hats." A Bitcoin Policy Institute lawyer offered to talk.
  • Yan's verdict on the hat color: gray. Taking everything to beat a black hat is arguable. Keeping a cut is not. "You don't just return a wallet and take a bunch of stuff out of it."
  • Suze's question: Bitcoiners are ruthless about added trust assumptions, so why did Liquid get a pass? "Were we discerning enough?" Leave the base layer and you take on another code base and another set of failure points.
  • ⭐ Yan on open source in the AI era: it stays because every open project gets red-teamed by the whole internet. Closed systems get hacked too, "we just don't hear about them." The base chain is "the ultimate boss" nobody has beaten.
  • Yan's bank numbers, read live from the Identity Theft Resource Center: 3,332 reported data compromises in 2025 affecting 280 million people, 739 of them in financial services. "Bank-grade security" is not a standard anyone actually meets.
  • ⭐ Frank's hard question: must the layers be as bulletproof as Bitcoin? Yan: nothing is, and the only path is slow growth. Bitcoin was attacked at $1, then $10,000, then a billion. Early adopters carry the risk.
  • Yan's rocket-ship rule. Bitcoin Core engineering is closer to launching a spacecraft than shipping web software. "Years of careful review, study, simulations on other chains." Test new tech on other coins for two years first.
  • Suze asked whether ossification risks losing the skills to change Bitcoin in 50 years. Frank and Yan: no. Ossification is no new features, not no developers, and AI has widened who can work on cryptography and game theory.
  • Yan on open-weight versus hosted AI: the same debate as open source versus closed, and open source won the internet. His advice to companies: externalize memory, skills and harness so you can swap models. Swan built its own.
  • Unseen Finance returned with a proposal: these incidents are a credibility problem for the services on top of Bitcoin, not for Bitcoin. His fix, borrowed from banking: a self-regulatory body plus an insurance pool that service providers pay into.
  • Brady's tally at the close: Cory, Yan, Steve, Alec, Isaiah, Matt and Brandon from Swan; Larry Lepard three times; Parker Lewis, Daniel Batten, Tom and Callum, Guy Swann, Ryan MacLeod, Alana, Bob Burnett, Roxana. Suze made 35 of 37.
  • The close. "We have the tools, we have the knowledge, we have the culture, we have the determination." The half-price buy fee ends today; limit orders placed today keep it. Yan's last word: take security seriously, "go play with AI."
    • ]]>

item.title: Bitcoiners - Live From Bitcoin Beach – This French Family Sold Everything, Moved to El Salvador and Started a Business in El Zonte | Antoine Allain of La Cajita Kitchen
item.description:
What happens when a nightclub bouncer from Santa Barbara, California sells everything he owns and opens a restaurant in El Zonte?

You’ve probably seen Max Keiser posting from a beach restaurant and wondered how it got there. The posts show the finished version. They don’t show the ten years before it, or the little box it started in.

Mike sits down with Antoine Allain, owner of La Cajita, born in Brittany, France, raised in California from age 13, and a former competitive surfer who first came to El Zonte about 10 years ago on a surf trip.

He fell for the town in half an hour, surfed, and went home. Three years ago he came back with his dad for a birthday trip and found a different place, with more energy and more room to start something. On the first day they were already talking about what they could open here. Antoine called his wife and told her he thought they were moving to El Salvador. Her answer wasn’t yes. He tells you how she came around, and which part of living in El Salvador was hardest for her to get used to.

They sold everything in France and California and opened in a tiny box on the sand, serving the crepes and galettes his dad cooks at home. The risk sat on Antoine alone. One ingredient is hard to find in the country, so friends bring it in by the bag.

Then a smash burger went on the menu and the little box filled up. Then Max came to eat, became a partner, and the move upstairs that followed brought a crowd that still fills the place every night of rainy season. Antoine is clear about one thing: Max checks in on the numbers like a businessman, and the growth came bigger than they’d expected.

Antoine knew nothing about Bitcoin when he opened. Hear what accepting it has done for his customer count and for the kind of people who walk through the door.

He and Mike also get into El Salvador surf from a local’s view: the two peaks he rotates through on the El Zonte surf calendar, and La Cajita Express, the contest he runs where 20 men and five women competed for $1,250.

If you’re one of the El Salvador expats wondering how the town treats a foreigner opening a business, Mike asks him directly. His answer is short and worth hearing from him.

A family bet everything on a small box on the beach and El Zonte showed up for them!

Whether you’re weighing a business of your own in El Salvador or you want to know what’s behind the burger Mike keeps ordering, listen to this one.


—Bitcoin Beach Team

item.title: The Bitcoin Frontier – Inside Wall Street’s bitcoin playbook with Denny Galindo
item.description:
Denny is a wealth manager and bitcoin research lead at Morgan Stanley, where he bridges traditional finance and bitcoin for high-net-worth investors. He operates inside one of the world’s largest financial institutions while developing frameworks to help advisors understand and allocate to bitcoin.

In this episode, Denny joins The Bitcoin Frontier to share how investors should think about bitcoin in a portfolio, the three core investor buckets driving adoption, and his thoughts on determining whether you’re underweight or overweight bitcoin. We dig into bitcoin’s market cycles and seasonal framework, the role of global money supply in driving returns, and practical strategies for gaining exposure in a volatile asset.

item.title: BITCOIN & ALTCOINS – Bitcoin und Altcoins: Wo sich jetzt Chancen eröffnen könnten
item.description:
Bitcoin und viele Altcoins stehen seit Wochen unter Druck. Die wiederkehrenden Rücksetzer zehren an den Nerven – und die Euphorie nach dem Sprung über 80.000 Dollar ist inzwischen deutlich abgeklungen. Doch können gerade solche Phasen auch Hinweise auf einen möglichen Ausbruch liefern? In unserem Podcast „Bitcoin und Altcoins“ spricht Oliver Michel von der tokentus investment AG darüber, welche Impulse Konjunkturdaten und die laufende Berichtssaison bringen könnten – und warum sich manche Coins der allgemeinen Marktrichtung entziehen.

Hinweis: Die im Podcast besprochenen Coins und Token stellen keine spezifischen Kauf- oder Anlageempfehlungen dar. Die Moderatoren oder der Verlag haften nicht für etwaige Verluste, die aufgrund der Umsetzung der im Podcast diskutierten Gedanken oder Ideen entstehen.

Das Gespräch wurde am 27.10.2026 an der Frankfurter Börse aufgezeichnet.

Tägliche Informationen gefällig? Dann ab zu „Krypto-Insights“ – dem Telegram-Kanal von Oliver Michel und Johanna Krämer. Weitere Infos unter www.krypto-insights.de

item.title: THE Bitcoin Podcast – Bitcoin’s Disbelief Rally: Who Is Left to Sell? | James Check & Michael Sullivan
item.description:
Who is left to sell Bitcoin?

James Check (Checkmate) and Michael Sullivan are back for round two after Peak Apathy. We put Check’s on-chain analysis alongside Michael’s language-based sentiment research to explore the gap between Bitcoin’s recovering price and the crowd’s lingering disbelief.

Check explains his seller-exhaustion thesis and why a calendar is no substitute for studying how holders behave. Michael breaks down excitement, desire, fear and anger—and why hoping for a higher price is not the same as buying Bitcoin.

We also discuss coin age and spending behavior, DCA versus emotional buying, how to measure Bitcoin’s returns, and why quieter Bitcoiners may simply be busy building businesses and raising families. Then we zoom out to adoption “one funeral at a time,” shifting narratives, AI, scarcity, and the history embedded in Bitcoin’s UTXO set.

Both guests remain bullish, but their thesis is not a guarantee: Check allows for another selloff, and Michael explicitly separates his long-term conviction from the next two weeks.

Recorded October 19, 2026.

item.title: No Second Best - A Bitcoin Podcast – Did the Federal Reserve Just Open the Door to Bitcoin?
item.description:
Jamie Dimon just went on national television to push back against Bitcoin and crypto legislation. Hours later, a Bitcoin exchange gained direct access to the Federal Reserve's settlement rails.

At the same time, Morgan Stanley filed for a spot Bitcoin ETF while geopolitical tensions escalated in the Middle East and Bitcoin surged.

This episode breaks down the growing conflict between the traditional banking system and the emerging Bitcoin financial infrastructure, and why the global monetary system may already be bending toward neutral, hard money.

item.title: Thank God for Bitcoin – TGFB Episode 83: A Candid Conversation with Rapper and Truth-Teller, Zuby
item.description:
Zuby (@ZubyMusic) joins Jordan Bush for a wide-ranging conversation about faith, courage, and what it takes to be a positive voice in a divided world. He tells the story of his path from independent rapper to one of today's most recognizable social commentators, and how the COVID era pushed him to start speaking out. He also reflects on the upbringing that shaped his character.

From there, Zuby and Jordan dig into the ideologies shaping public discourse: gender norms, privilege, victim mentality, and the grievance culture that keeps people divided. Zuby makes the case for empowerment over resentment, for solutions over complaints, and for a sturdier definition of love and care. He closes by sharing how his faith has grown, why he worries about the UK's loss of national pride and purpose, and why he still believes optimism and individual responsibility can change things.

Rapper. Author. Speaker. Coach. Host @ZubyPodcast

'Strong Advice' book https://zubymusic.gumroad.com/l/zubyfitness

]]>

item.title: Bitcoin.com News Interviews – Stanyakin, ChangeNOW Head of Growt: Trust, Compliance and the Crypto Super App
item.description:
What does it take for a crypto company to earn trust when things go wrong?


Tim Stanyakin, Head of Growth at ChangeNOW, joins Matthew Owens at TOKEN2049. He traces ChangeNOW from a 2017 swap service to a crypto super app, and explains why crypto and traditional finance will collaborate rather than compete, and how compliance and security build user confidence.

Topics covered:

  • Building a crypto super app around what users ask for
  • On- and off-ramps under tighter regulation
  • TradFi on crypto rails, US policy and MiCA in Europe
  • KYB/KYC, address scoring, AML partners and licensed custody
  • Crisis response, Bybit, and ChangeNOW's nine-year no-hack claim
  • Tokenized real-world assets and privacy vs compliance

item.title: House of Satoshi - Bitcoin und Friends – #67 Zana Iseni: Bankerin am Tag, Bitcoinerin in der Nacht
item.description:
Zana Iseni wollte ihrem Partner Bitcoin ausreden und hat sich dabei selbst überzeugt. 2016 schickte sie ihm noch einen Artikel über «gefährliche Kryptowährungen», heute ist Bitcoin ihre grösste Leidenschaft.


Tagsüber arbeitet Zana in Risk Control und regulatorischem Reporting einer Bank. Abends ist sie Mrs. Zatoshi: Bitcoin-Educatorin auf Instagram und LinkedIn, Keynote-Speakerin und Mitgründerin von Satoshis Daughters.


Mit Rino spricht sie über teures Lerngeld, über Bitcoin für Einsteiger und darüber, warum sie beim Wallet-Setup sogar die Brille abzieht.

  • Bitcoin speichert Lebenszeit: Lohn ist das Ladegerät, Fiat ein Akku, der in der Schublade leerläuft
  • Warum sie als Bankerin lange nicht über Bitcoin reden wollte
  • Buy the dip oder Sparplan? Was der Fear & Greed Index taugt
  • Seed Phrase selber würfeln, mit Bleistift aufschreiben, Setup nie verraten
  • Don’t trust, verify: die Sache mit dem Kokoswasser

item.title: The Bitcoin Infinity Show – Why Every Bitcoiner Needs Two Stacks | Matouš Ledvina | BIS #226
item.description:
Matouš Ledvina joins the Bitcoin Infinity Show to talk about leaving Google for freedom tech at Invity, SatoshiLabs’ MiCA-licensed Bitcoin-only app, and why the next wave of Bitcoin adoption means meeting newcomers where they are. He and Knut Svanholm make the case for keeping separate KYC and non-KYC stacks, moving coins into self-custody, and why Bitcoin treasury companies like Strategy may carry far more hidden risk than their buyers realize. They also dig into the fiat endgame, the dollar’s slow decline, and what it takes to build regulated Bitcoin products in Europe.

item.title: Bitcoin Audible – Everything Is a Lie (Inflation Edition)
item.description:
I break down four of the biggest lies we’re told about inflation, from the idea that prices must always rise to the fantasy that GDP growth means we’re getting richer. I show how money printing, cheap debt, and fake economic metrics quietly transfer real wealth from workers and savers to the already powerful. If you’ve ever wondered why everything feels more expensive and more fragile, this is a quick demolition of the stories we’ve been sold.

Chapters

(00:00:00) - Introduction

(00:00:21) - Everything should always get more affordable

(00:01:16) - Corporate greed cannot cause real inflation

(00:02:42) - Inflation only hurts the economy

(00:04:16) - GDP is not a useful metric

(00:05:37) - Closing thoughts

item.title: Bitcoin Insights | Bitcoin Podcast mit Philipp 'PJAH' Hartmannsgruber – #16 Im Auto nach El Zonte: Bitcoin in El Salvador mit Robin Seyr und Ben Raich
item.description:
In dieser Episode spricht Philipp mit Robin Seyr und Ben Raich im Auto auf dem Weg von San Salvador nach El Zonte über ihre Eindrücke aus El Salvador. Sie diskutieren die Bitcoin-Adoption, die Adopting Bitcoin-Konferenz, die Sicherheitslage, die alltägliche Nutzung von Bitcoin und die politische Situation unter Präsident Bukele.


Wer ist Robin Seyr?

item.title: Bitcoin Audible – Everything Is a Lie (Inflation Edition)
item.description:
I break down four of the biggest lies we’re told about inflation, from the idea that prices must always rise to the fantasy that GDP growth means we’re getting richer. I show how money printing, cheap debt, and fake economic metrics quietly transfer real wealth from workers and savers to the already powerful. If you’ve ever wondered why everything feels more expensive and more fragile, this is a quick demolition of the stories we’ve been sold.

Chapters

(00:00:00) - Introduction

(00:00:21) - Everything should always get more affordable

(00:01:16) - Corporate greed cannot cause real inflation

(00:02:42) - Inflation only hurts the economy

(00:04:16) - GDP is not a useful metric

(00:05:37) - Closing thoughts

item.title: BitcoinBázis - Minden, Ami Kriptó – Így Detektálod az Insidereket On-chain Adatokkal – InsightX Interjú Szathmáry Zsófival
item.description:
🚀 A BitcoinBázis podcast eheti műsorában vendégünk Szathmáry Zsófi az InsightX-től!

Hogyan jutott el egy biomérnök PhD-s a laborból a kripto on-chain elemzés világába? Zsófival beszélgetünk az InsightX történetéről, az Atlas Live holder térképről, a memecoin-trenches rizikóiról, a hideg megkeresés (cold outreach) titkairól 2026-ban, a női reprezentációról a kriptóban, valamint arról, miért kell kritikusan olvasni a kripto Twittert.

Ha érdekel, hogyan lehet jobban navigálni a scam-ek és insiderek között valódi on-chain adatokkal, ezt a részt ne hagyd ki! 🔥👀


⏱️ Időbélyegek:


00:00 - 00:19 Intro

00:20 - 01:41 Zsófi útja a laborból az üzleti architektúrába

01:42 - 04:04 Hogyan került a kriptóba és az InsightX-be?

04:05 - 06:01 Mi az az InsightX és milyen problémát old meg?

06:02 - 08:42 Atlas Live holder map + decentralization score

08:43 - 12:02 On-chain adatok, kontextus és KOL-tárca label-ek

12:03 - 16:16 Cold outreach tippek 2026-ban (személyre szabott üzenetek + vizuális elemek)

16:17 - 17:04 FireFish

19:42 - 25:23 A legfontosabb Business Development-készségek: türelem és kitartás

25:24 - 29:08 Stakeholder management: nagy tanácsadó cég vs. lean startup

29:09 - 31:04 Kockázatok a crypto analytics szektorban (trendek + reguláció)

31:05 - 33:22 Következő mérföldkövek: prediction markets + intézményi irány

33:23 - 40:59 Orange pill moment + trading tapasztalatok és taktikák

41:00 - 44:04 Női reprezentáció a tudományban, mérnökségben és a kriptóban

44:05 - 44:37 Bitpanda

44:38 - 52:50 Tanácsok pályakezdőknek (tapasztalat, network, proaktivitás)

52:51 - 54:39 Záró gondolatok + hol találkozhatsz az InsightX-szel

🔗https://www.linkedin.com/in/zsofia-szathmary/

🔗App: app.insightx.network

🔗X: x.com/InsightXnetwork

#BitcoinBázis #InsightX #CryptoAnalytics #OnChain #AtlasLive #HolderMap #Memecoins #Trenches #BusinessDevelopment #ColdOutreach #NőkAKriptóban #Web3 #Solana #PumpFun #CryptoTwitter #CryptoPodcast #bitcoinpodcast


📌A műsorban elhangzó szakszavak magyarázatát itt találod:

👉Futures: hagyományos határidős ügyletek (van lejáratuk).

👉Perps (vagy perpetual futures) = lejárat nélküli határidős ügyletek.

👉Mémcoin trenches: a frissen indított, nagyon kockázatos mémcoinok kaotikus kereskedési környezete👉Cold outreach: olyan üzleti vagy kapcsolatépítési célú megkeresés, amelyet olyan személynek küldesz, akivel korábban még semmilyen kapcsolatod nem volt.

👉Lead-to-partner pipeline: az a strukturált üzleti folyamat, amely során a potenciális, jelölteket szisztematikus megkeresésekkel, szűrésekkel hivatalos, együttműködő partnerekké vagy értékesítési csatornákká alakítják át.

👉Pump.fun: egy Solana-alapú kriptoplatform

👉Axiom: egy rendkívül népszerű, decentralizált on-chain kereskedési terminál és bot

👉GMGN: egyik legnépszerűbb on-chain elemző- és kereskedési felület

item.title: The Peter McCormack Show – #224 - Frank Wright - The Debt Trap: Inflation, Falling Living Standards & Our Children’s Future
item.description:
Why does working harder no longer feel like getting ahead? Frank Wright returns to discuss Britain’s debt-driven economy, inflation and the squeeze on living standards. We explore his argument that financial power has become detached from productive wealth, while households face rising costs and the next generation inherits the bill.


We discuss central banking, the offshoring of industry, housing costs and student debt, before turning to what rebuilding Britain would involve: cheaper energy, domestic production, skilled work and a long-term national strategy.


- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

item.title: VERIFIED by Bitcoin Suisse – He Co-Wrote the Paper Behind Modern AI. Then Built NEAR
item.description:
His grandparents' life savings ended up in a Soviet bank book that became worthless. As a kid in Ukraine, he watched bread prices rise exponentially. Years later he co-authored the paper behind modern AI, and he's convinced AI and crypto belong together. 

Illia Polosukhin, co-author of "Attention Is All You Need" and co-founder of NEAR, joins Bitcoin Suisse to explain how the transformer actually works, why he left Google to start NEAR as an AI company in 2017, and why he thinks we've done almost nothing to prepare our systems for a post-AGI world.

item.title: POD256 | Bitcoin Mining, Freedom Tech, and Awesome Tangents – 130. Cyber Attacktober: When the Internet’s Trust Model Breaks
item.description:
In this episode, we dug into what felt like a nonstop wave of security incidents across the internet and Bitcoin-adjacent tools, from wallet breaches and phishing concerns to major vulnerabilities in PHP and Tailscale. We unpacked why this moment feels different: smaller bugs with massive consequences, faster exploitation cycles, and the growing role of open-weight AI models in both attack and defense. We also explored how many users are stuck depending on banks, governments, hosting providers, and app stores to patch critical systems for them—and why that lack of control should concern all of us.

We also spent time on one of the wildest stories of the week: the eMudhra certificate authority failure, where disastrously weak keys briefly undermined core internet trust assumptions and opened the door to man-in-the-middle risks until browsers and apps revoked trust. From there, we zoomed out into the bigger picture: smart TVs and IoT devices spying on users, insecure home networks, the value of open-source firmware, and how AI agents may soon mediate more of our digital lives. The thread running through the whole conversation was clear: if we want privacy, resilience, and real autonomy, we need transparent systems we can audit, control, and update on our own terms.

]]>

item.title: The Bitcoin Boomers – Don’t Use Ledger.
item.description:
Someone put a chip inside the hardware wallet. Then they waited. George Bodine walks through the Ledger reseller attack, the 2020 breach Ledger said hit about 10,000 customers (the leaked database had 272,000 names and home addresses), and why he's been throwing Ledgers in the trash for years. Bob Burnett explains the part everyone gets wrong: Bitcoin didn't fail, the things you plug into it did. Larry Lepard on 1933, phishing, the deepfake phone call he's waiting for, and why he wipes his Trezor after every use.

Then Bob previews something he's been building: a way to send a transaction that the world can't see until it's already in a block.

CHAPTERS

00:00 welcome, and a toast to the one kid who listened

00:43 a maxi with bitcoin in more than one bucket

02:28 the ledger reseller story

03:43 they waited

04:32 the 2020 breach, 10,000 vs 272,000

05:35 the fendi wallet

06:33 bob: bitcoin didn't fail, the interface did

07:57 two of three, geographically dispersed

09:22 the etf question

10:41 what if the government says it's illegal

11:25 opsec vs complexity

11:45 the coldcard entropy scare

13:09 why larry still runs single sig on a trezor

13:50 phishing, deepfakes, and the call from your kid

15:53 don't keep it in the house, wipe the device

17:58 bob's pre-announcement: replace by fee as an attack

22:10 private transaction submission

23:56 what to tell the golfing buddy with a million

26:17 self custody is not as easy as driving a car

27:41 let the hate mail come in

SPONSORS

Swan, Bitcoin only, recurring buys, withdraw to self custody. https://swan.com/boomers\

Sazmining, you own the rig, power at cost, coins go to your wallet. https://sazmining.com/boomers\

The Bitcoin Boomers is a panel for smart, successful people over 40 still on the outside of Bitcoin looking in. Plain English answers to the questions no one else will touch. Signal without the noise.

Your hosts:

Gary Leland, founder of BitBlockBoom

Lawrence Lepard, sound money fund manager and author of The Big Print.

Bob Burnett, mining entrepreneur and founder of Barefoot Mining.

George Bodine, the World's Most Interesting Bitcoiner.

Listen to the audio anywhere:

Subscribe: https://www.youtube.com/@BTCBoomers\

item.title: 21Focus - Der Bitcoin-Unternehmer Podcast – Aus der Banken IT in die Welt von Bitcoin - Harald Betz
item.description:
Folge #61 – Ein Gespräch über Banken IT und Bitcoin Bücher

Harald Beetz ist seit fast 20 Jahren selbstständig in der Beratung für Banken und Rechenzentren. Angefangen als Banklehrling bei der Sparkasse, hat er früh den Wandel von Beratung hin zu reinem Vertrieb erlebt und sich auf IT-Projekte spezialisiert. In diesem Gespräch erzählt er, wie er von der Banken IT zu Bitcoin kam, warum er mit seiner Frau einen Roman über Geld schrieb und wie er sich heute zwischen Beratung und Content rund um Bitcoin positioniert.


Du erfährst,

  • wie Harald die Bankenwelt von innen erlebt hat,
  • welche Herausforderungen und Chancen es als IT-Berater gibt,
  • warum er Bitcoin zunächst wieder verkaufte und später mit völlig anderem Blick neu entdeckte,
  • wie aus einer Buchidee seiner Frau ein gemeinsames Projekt wurde
  • und welche unternehmerischen Lektionen er aus fast zwei Jahrzehnten Selbstständigkeit mitnimmt.


Kapitel:

  • 00:00 Begrüßung und Vorstellung
  • 02:15 Vom Banklehrling zum IT-Berater
  • 07:40 Veränderungen in der Bankenwelt seit den 2000er Jahren
  • 15:10 Einstieg in die Selbstständigkeit und erste Projekte
  • 22:05 Gescheiterte Produktidee und der Wechsel zur Beratung
  • 29:15 Erster Kontakt mit Bitcoin und die zweite Begegnung
  • 36:50 Der Roman über Geld und Bitcoin
  • 44:20 Zukunft der Beratung im Banken- und Bitcoin-Umfeld
  • 49:00 Wichtigste Tipps für Vertrieb und Resilienz

LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/haraldbetz

item.title: Bitcoin für Frauen – Folge 8 – Bitcoin in Prozent: Was Rendite, Gewinn und Verlust wirklich bedeuten
item.description:
Wie viel sind eigentlich 100 Prozent Gewinn? Warum braucht man nach 50 Prozent Verlust wieder 100 Prozent Gewinn, um beim Ausgangswert anzukommen? Und was bedeutet es, wenn bei Bitcoin von einer durchschnittlichen jährlichen Wachstumsrate von mehr als 70 Prozent gesprochen wird?

In dieser Folge schauen wir uns die Bitcoin-Kursentwicklung einmal nicht in Dollar oder Euro, sondern in Prozent an.

Ich erkläre euch anhand einfacher Beispiele, wie sich Gewinne und Verluste berechnen, warum Prozentzahlen über mehrere Jahre nicht einfach addiert werden können und was hinter Begriffen wie Rendite oder annualisierter Wachstumsrate steckt.

Außerdem vergleichen wir die historische Bitcoin-Entwicklung mit einem klassischen Bankzins und schauen uns an, warum diese beiden Dinge zwar nicht dasselbe sind, der Vergleich aber trotzdem hilft, die Größenordnungen besser zu verstehen.

Wir sprechen über die Auswertungen von Fidelity Digital Assets und Glassnode und darüber, was die bisherigen Bitcoin-Jahre tatsächlich gezeigt haben.

Und ganz wichtig: Es geht nicht darum, zukünftige Renditen vorherzusagen, sondern darum, vergangene Entwicklungen richtig lesen und einordnen zu können.

Wie immer gilt: Dieser Podcast dient ausschließlich der Wissensvermittlung rund um Bitcoin und stellt keine Anlage- oder Finanzberatung dar. Bitte überprüft meine Aussagen selbst und bildet euch eure eigene Meinung.

]]>

item.title: 21talk – JP Morgan Prognose: Bitcoin vor Gold & Aktien | 21weekly mit Chris/ @coinjoined
item.description:
In diesem 21weekly spricht Dino Heinert (21bitcoin) mit Gast und Sicherheitsexperte Chris (Seedor & Bitsurance), der sich live vom Plan B Forum in Lugano meldet, über aktuelle Sicherheitsrisiken bei der Bitcoin Self-Custody. Im Fokus stehen jüngste Hardware-Wallet-Hacks und Supply-Chain-Angriffe, bei denen selbst manipulierte Sicherheitschips zum Einsatz kamen. Chris und Dino erklären verständlich, worauf Krypto-Anleger beim Kauf von Wallets achten müssen und wie man die eigene Seed Phrase durch Praxislösungen wie eine Passphrase (25. Wort), Multisig oder neue Technologien wie Frostsnap optimal gegen Totalverlust und Diebstahl schützt.Außerdem diskutieren Dino und Chris die neuesten Entwicklungen im institutionellen Finanzsektor und deren Auswirkungen auf den Bitcoin-Markt. Sie analysieren die Pläne der Sparkasse zum Bitcoin-Verkauf, anhaltende Rekord-Zuflüsse in Bitcoin Spot ETFs sowie die bemerkenswerte Prognose von JP Morgan, wonach Bitcoin als Assetklasse aktuell vor Gold und Aktien liegt. Welche geopolitischen Chancen und Risiken dieser Wettlauf um BTC zwischen den USA und Europa birgt, erfährst du in dieser ausführlichen Marktanalyse.Chris: https://x.com/coinjoined21Insights: https://21bitcoin.app/blog/21insights-europas-neue-bitcoin-ordnung

(00:00) Intro & Themenüberblick (00:41) Chris live vom Plan B Forum in Lugano (01:53) Hardware-Wallet-Hacks & Ledger Supply-Chain-Attacke (06:05) Wie sicher ist Self-Custody noch? (Tipps für Einsteiger & Multisig) (08:44) Passphrase & Frostsnap (13:19) Sparkasse verkauft Bitcoin: Was steckt dahinter? (18:04) Bitcoin Spot-ETFs: Neue Rekord-Zuflüsse & Zulassung in der Schweiz (21:21) JP Morgan Prognose: Bitcoin schlägt Gold & Aktien (25:04) Bitcoin-Wettlauf: USA vs. Europa (26:44) Fazit & Verabschiedung

Welche geopolitischen Chancen und Risiken dieser Wettlauf um BTC zwischen den USA und Europa birgt, erfährst du in dieser ausführlichen Marktanalyse.Chris: https://x.com/coinjoined21Insights: https://21bitcoin.app/blog/21insights-europas-neue-bitcoin-ordnung

item.title: Epicenter - Learn about Crypto, Blockchain, Ethereum, Bitcoin and Distributed Technologies – The DAO Security Fund: Turning a Historic Hack into Ethereum's Future | Griff Green
item.description:
Ten years after The DAO hack changed Ethereum forever, Griff Green returns to Epicenter to discuss the next chapter: the DAO Security Fund.


As a co-initiator of The DAO, Griff shares the untold story of recovering funds after the hack, why over 75,000 ETH remained untouched for years, and how its staking yield is now funding public goods for Ethereum security. The conversation also explores a provocative idea: Ethereum is incredibly secure—but still not safe for everyday users.


Topics covered:

1. The inside story of The DAO and its recovery

2. Why the DAO hack may be the only hack where everyone made money

3. The DAO Security Fund and funding Ethereum security

4. Quadratic funding, grants & public goods

5. Why phishing and UX remain Ethereum's biggest weakness

6. Can Ethereum become safer than traditional banks?

7. The future of safer wallets, OpSec, and the Ethereum Economic Zone


If you enjoyed the episode, don't forget to subscribe for more conversations with the builders, founders and investors shaping the future of crypto.

item.title: HashrateUp - A Bitcoin Mining Podcast – Hashprice Is Going to $80. Here’s Why.
item.description:
Is hashrate the next major commodity? Francisco Quadrio Monteiro (BD & Strategy at POW.RE) joins Jesse to break down how a Bitcoin hashrate OTC desk prices risk, who is buying hashrate today, and why hashprice could land around $70–80 within the next 12 months.


Since leaving Paraguay, POW.RE has shifted to trading physically delivered hashrate. Francisco explains why difficulty is now the only real risk factor in BTC-denominated contracts, why past data is a poor guide in today's market, and why Bitcoin treasury companies like Strategy should be deploying capital into mining.


TIMESTAMPS:

0:00 Introduction

1:21 How POW.RE got its name

2:15 From Paraguay to hashrate trading

3:37 Modeling difficulty: the secret sauce

8:11 Francisco's call: $70–80 hashprice in 12 months

8:49 Why each new megawatt moves difficulty less

10:02 Hashprice in BTC vs USD terms

10:55 Where unplugged ASICs are going

13:12 What matters most in a hashrate contract

14:51 Who's buying hashrate right now

16:22 Hosting providers buying hashrate for uptime

17:56 The eCash hard fork explained

20:10 Mining + DCA: lower-volatility accumulation

23:32 Why you should pay your hosting bill weekly

32:04 Why the ability to spend Bitcoin matters

34:38 Block space is as scarce as Bitcoin

35:29 Lightning, stablecoins & the security budget

36:39 Block space forward markets

37:23 Making solo mining more exciting

41:29 Lightning payouts straight from the pool

43:09 Orange-pilling Dad with an S9 heater

44:34 Business ideas & the future of FPPS pools

46:48 Outro


KEY TOPICS:

• Hashrate as a commodity and BTC-denominated contracts

• Hashprice outlook and difficulty modeling

• Who buys hashrate: fork speculators, political signaling, hosting providers

• Mining + DCA as a lower-volatility accumulation strategy

• Block space scarcity, Lightning payouts and the mining x gambling crossover

item.title: Bitcoin Country Podcast – Julian Liniger, Max & Stacy: how El Salvador is the new Switzerland
item.description:
Got something to say to this podcast? Send a voicemail, and you might hear yourself on the next episode!

Julian Liniger is the co-founder and CEO of Relai, the biggest Bitcoin-only exchange in Europe, founded in Zurich in 2020, which has helped more than 100,000 people buy over 20,000 bitcoin straight into self-custody.

This conversation on X Spaces yesterday with Julian, Max Keiser, Stacy Herbert, and moderator Jethro Toro covered...

  • Julian’s decade in Bitcoin: buying his first coin through a friend in 2015, the 2017 Silicon Valley gold rush, and founding Relai in 2020
  • Why Relai went Bitcoin-only: listening to the Bitcoin community, standing for one thing as a brand, and still turning down investors who want other coins
  • Relai by the numbers: around $1.5 billion in volume, 650,000 app downloads, 80% of orders through DCA savings plans, and every bitcoin sent straight to users’ own wallets
  • Bitcoin in Europe today: KYC-free onboarding in Switzerland until 2024, the cost of a MiCA license, and how a bear market changes retail behavior
  • Who is adopting, and why: savers who know fiat is broken, an average user age of 43, high-net-worth clients, and businesses putting Bitcoin on their balance sheet
  • Max and Stacy on the early days in Europe: the hacker community, the Keiser Report, and why El Salvador stays the only true Bitcoin Country
  • From low trust to high trust: Stacy on El Salvador’s transformation, CUBO+ education, and the comparison with Switzerland
  • Bitcoin Histórico: a preview of Julian’s keynote “El Salvador Is the Next Switzerland”, on stability, security, beauty and sound money foundations, in El Salvador’s National Palace

Join us for the full Freedom Month experience this November:

📍 10th · Bitcoin Capital Summit

📍 11 & 12 · BitcoinHistorico.com (use code “COWBOY21” for 21% off)

📍 13th · Renaissance Rodeo

📍 18 & 19 · EmTech AI Conference

📍 19 & 20 · Global Bitcoin Circular Economies Summit

You can check out the original Space here:

https://x.com/i/spaces/1oKMvNobgmRGQ?s=20

https://x.com/Relai_app

https://x.com/maxkeiser

item.title: HUSZONEGY Bitcoin podcast – Bitcoin vs kripto: mit nem tud a proof of stake?
item.description:
Egy nézői kérdésre sorra vesszük, mi a különbség a proof of work és a proof of stake között, és miért itt válnak el a bitcoinerek a kriptósoktól. Egy olimpiai hasonlattal megmutatjuk, hogyan dönt a pénz az Ethereumban, és azt is, miért nem ad a Bitcoinban több hatalmat a nagy vagyon. Szó esik a Ledger-hackről, egy indiai tanúsítványkiadó hibájáról, amely miatt bármelyik weboldal hamisítható lett, és arról, mikor jelenthet valódi veszélyt a kvantumszámítógép. A végén bemutatjuk az Umbrel 2.0-t, amellyel felhasználóbarát módon futtathatod a saját Bitcoin node-odat.


FEJEZETEK:

00:00 Proof of stake olimpia (Intro)

02:19 Kémchipet építettek a Ledgerbe

06:34 Nincs tuti recept a védekezésre

09:13 Miért nem árulunk hardvertárcát?

11:53 Hamisítható lett bármelyik weboldal

17:17 A kvantumgép még a 16-ot sem bontja fel

21:34 Kell internet a Bitcoinhoz?

24:52 Proof of work: véletlen, amit senki nem irányít

28:51 Az áram maga a bizonyíték

33:22 Vitalik ötlete: tegyük le az árát

36:08 Bitcoinban a pénz nem ad hatalmat

38:44 Miért nem lesz másik Bitcoin?

42:06 Umbrel 2.0, ami már nem fagy le

47:20 Vége a bear marketnek?


FORRÁSOK:

Umbrel ➡ https://umbrel.com

Saját Bitcoin node ➡ https://bitcoinmentor.hu/sajat-bitcoin-node/

Bitcoin Miskolc konferencia, november 20–22. ➡ https://bitcoinmiskolc.hu

Bitcoin multisig és öröklés ➡ https://bitcoinmentor.hu/bitcoin-multisig-es-orokles/

item.title: Natalie Brunell's Coin Stories – SPECIAL REPORT: Social Security Is Running Out of Money. What Happens Next?
item.description:
We've been paying into Social Security our entire working lives. But the retirement trust fund is projected to run dry in 2032, and millions of Americans could face a 22% cut in benefits if Congress doesn't act.

So where did all that money go?

In this special episode, I break down how Social Security really works, why it's running short on money, and how Washington ended up making trillions in promises it hasn't fully funded.

I also get into the looming Medicare crisis, the growing burden on younger generations, and why the decisions Washington makes could affect not just your retirement benefits, but the purchasing power of your money.

item.title: Bright Orange Future – Leigh Cuen: Poet Journalist #010
item.description:
They’re back! The Brothers Klippsten reunite after a two month hiatus. They're joined by seasoned writer and journalist, Leigh Cuen. The gang discusses journalism and how technology has changed legacy media models, creativity in the open-source space, objective reporting, culture shock, and Bitcoin’s impact on a global scale.

Leigh has been busy! She's covered culture, data journalism, social analysis, Bitcoin, human rights, technology, and multimedia production, and is co-founder of ONA Jerusalem, the first Online News Association group in the Middle East.

Her work has been featured in publications such as Newsweek Japan, International Business Times, Racked, CoinDesk, Insider, History Today, Mic, Al Jazeera, YNet, The Jerusalem Post, Mic, and Salon. Leigh’s work has also been published in Spanish, French, Italian, Hebrew and Arabic.

item.title: Finanzielle Intelligenz mit Marc Friedrich – Erbschaftsteuer-Reform: Was die SPD plant und wie die Union reagiert
item.description:
Stephan Reinholz ist Rechtsanwalt, Fachanwalt für Erbrecht und Fachanwalt für Steuerrecht sowie zertifizierter Stiftungsberater. Mit seiner Kanzlei Bärenweiler & Reinholz in Hamburg berät er Familien und Unternehmer bei Erbschaft, Schenkung und Unternehmensnachfolge.Im Gespräch geht es um das Verfahren vor dem Bundesverfassungsgericht zur steuerlichen Begünstigung von Betriebsvermögen: Warum ein Privaterbe zahlt, während Firmenerben steuerfrei bleiben können, welche Freibeträge und Steuersätze gelten und was ein Wegfall der Verschonung für Unternehmer bedeuten würde. Wir sprechen über das Beispiel Schweden, die Pläne der SPD, die Rolle der Union, den aktuellen Run auf Familienstiftungen und darüber, warum es sich lohnen kann, die Nachfolge jetzt anzugehen.


Hier gehts zum Video: https://youtu.be/I0jVdVsxsik

]]>
